Human and AI turns in vibe-coding sessions

Source: R/data-human_ai.R
human_ai.Rd

human_ai is a coded dataset of the turns in 429 human-AI pair-programming ("vibe coding") sessions in 34 projects, held between 5 February and 8 March 2026. The data are the standard example for a heterogeneous transition network with two actor types: six human codes (Check, Frustrate, Inquire, Refine, Request, Specify) and six AI codes (Ask, Delegate, Execute, Plan, Repair, Report). In each session a person directs an AI coding assistant; every turn is coded with one or more interaction codes, and the codes of both actors are interleaved in the order in which they occurred.

The codes are a simplified version of the original coding, with near-synonyms merged. AI codes: Investigate, Ask and Inquire became Ask; Explain and Report became Report. Human codes: Command and Request became Request; Correct and Verify became Check; Interrupt and Frustrate became Frustrate. The phase column splits the sessions into an early and a late half for grouped examples. The same rows are available split by actor type in human_simplified and ai_simplified, and the code-to-actor lookup in human_ai_codebook.

Usage

human_ai

Format

A data frame with 19,347 rows (10,796 human and 8,551 AI codes) and 11 columns, one row per code:

message_id

Integer identifier of the turn; the codes of one turn share it.

project

Project identifier, "Project_1" to "Project_34".

session_id

Session identifier (the session key for build_htna()).

timestamp

Integer Unix time of the session date (day resolution).

session_date

Date of the row, "YYYY-MM-DD".

code

Simplified interaction code.

cluster

High-level cluster of the original code, kept for reference; because merged codes may come from different clusters, one simplified code can carry more than one cluster label.

code_order

Order of the code within its turn.

order_in_session

Position of the row in its session, counting both actors (the order key for build_htna()).

actor_type

"Human" or "AI".

phase

Factor with levels "Early" and "Late": sessions ordered by their first date (session id breaking ties) and split in half, 214 early and 215 late sessions.

Source

Saqr, M. (2026). Human-AI vibe coding interaction study. https://saqr.me/blog/2026/human-ai-interaction-cograph/. Derived from the human_long and ai_long data of the 'Nestimate' package; the build script is data-raw/human_ai.R in the package sources.

See also

human_simplified, ai_simplified, human_ai_codebook, build_htna()

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
plot_htna(net)
